declaration.what: advance widths, in em, of HWP's own HFT faces
declaration.how: Widths[code] x FontMatrix[0], read out of the Type 3 font objects Hancom Office's own PDF export emits for a face it cannot embed, grouped by the HFT face the paired HWPX runs declare (hh:font@type="HFT")
declaration.source: the ten reference PDFs under tests/corpus/forms/render/, exported by Hancom Office
declaration.does_not_contain: no glyph outlines, no CharProcs streams, no font program, no font file, no byte of any Hancom font
declaration.legal: black-box output of a public document pipeline. Nothing here opens, reads or decompiles a Hancom font file; the numbers are the export's own declared advances, which any reader of those public PDFs can read the same way.

verification.what: the declared /Widths against the pen distance between two aligned glyph origins, on unstretched lines with no hh:spacing, per singleton segment
verification.note: a singleton's pen distance runs to the NEXT glyph's origin, so it still carries any gap Hancom opens at a class boundary; the residual is an upper bound

verification_in_table.what: the same reading, on the paragraphs INSIDE tables -- the rows the top-level walk above never reaches, which is where this table's 한양견고딕 and 8 pt 한양신명조 coverage comes from
verification_in_table.why_separate: advance_probe.probe_document walks the top-level paragraphs, because a cached hp:lineseg comparison is defined on the flowed body; the check above is read off it and is left exactly as it was
verification_in_table.note: read per class. digit, latin and punct -- the classes whose rows actually move an advance -- agree with /Widths to a few thousandths of an em. hangul does not: a cell line's pen distances run 4-5 % wide because the cell justifies its own text, which the top-level check never sees (hangul there is 0.0003 em). That costs this table nothing, because every hangul row it adds carries 1.0000 em -- exactly the declared cell an uncovered syllable already fell back to -- so no hangul row changes any advance the renderer computes.

declaration.hangul_fallback: a Hangul syllable this table does not cover is advanced by the declared cell; see the per-face hangul_em below

standin_declaration.what: advance widths, in em of the declared cell, of the faces this machine does NOT have installed and the renderer therefore substitutes
standin_declaration.how: the pen distance between two consecutive drawn glyph origins of one text-showing run in Hancom Office's own PDF export, divided by the run's declared cell; singleton segments only, no hh:spacing, run boundaries excluded
standin_declaration.why_not_the_font_object: a TTF-declared face reaches the export as an embedded subset TrueType, so reading its /W array would mean opening a font object. This measures ink positions on the page instead and never opens one.
standin_declaration.source: the ten reference PDFs under tests/corpus/forms/render/, exported by Hancom Office
standin_declaration.does_not_contain: no glyph outlines, no font program, no font file, no byte of any embedded font stream
standin_declaration.machine_dependent: which faces appear here is a property of the machine the table was measured on. The renderer gates the section on its own resolver's answer, so an installed face is never corrected by it.

HCI Poppy.substituted_because: the declared face is not installed on the machine this table was measured on; the resolver answered it from the bundled family map or the machine fallback
